svg.title: Gold indicator fits against BOTH approved gold pin sets — Set A (gold_v1, 6 pins) vs the algorithmic 20 (gold_v2, 15%)
svg.desc: IN-SAMPLE — a scoring target only, NOT a performance claim. Every separation is the MAXIMUM over a frozen grid, scored against cycle windows derived from the SAME price history the z-series are built from, so capture counts and depths are a partly-selected UPPER BOUND. No return / Sharpe / trade count is claimed on this figure.
svg.text: Gold indicator fits against BOTH approved gold pin sets — Set A (gold_v1, 6 pins) vs the algorithmic 20 (gold_v2, 15%)
GLD-USD · 2004-11-18..2026-09-29 (5499 daily bars) · capture bar 0.5 z-units on |separation| · dead zone ±0.06 · ±45d windows (all frozen; nothing tuned after seeing output)
HORIZONTAL BARS — one pair per indicator: gold_v1 on TOP, gold_v2 BELOW
Length = |separation|. RIGHT of zero = expected polarity (+1), LEFT and hatched = inverted (-1);
both bars of a pair are ONE indicator against the two approved pin sets. The grids, the 0.5 capture
bar, the 0.06 dead zone, the separation formula and the ±45d half-window are IDENTICAL between the
runs — only the window set differs.
VERDICT: gold_v1 fits BETTER — capture depth 21.5674 vs 11.4357 (margin -10.1317) on identical
headcount (10 vs 10). Depth, not headcount, is the ranking key.
VERDICT FLIPS between the pin sets: nfci (direction: +1.3157 → -0.6793), walcl (direction: -2.2117 →
+0.5042) — a flip is a change of capture or of fitted direction; a separation that merely moved is
GREEDY EQUAL-WEIGHT KEEP LIST: gold_v1 EMPTY (anchor-only) · gold_v2 EMPTY (anchor-only) — every
candidate made the anchor's own aggregate separation worse, so the frozen rule keeps none of them on
degenerate legs (excluded from every keep list): gvz, weekly_rsi, weekly_macd — a pass resting on a
dead side is not a pass, however deep it reads.
A filled diamond at a bar tip marks a CAPTURING leg; a hollow tip marks one that does not clear the
capture bar or rests on a dead side. The dashed vertical rules are the bar, drawn on both sides
PIN-SET INSET — windows asked about, what survived
separation (z), signed — the sign IS the direction
source: SdcaCycleWindows.gold_v1() and SdcaCycleWindows.gold_v2() / GLD-USD close column / 2004-11-18..2026-09-29 (5499 daily bars)
Both bars of a pair are ONE indicator scored against the two approved gold pin sets. The frozen grids, the 0.5 capture bar,
the 0.06 dead zone, the separation formula and the ±45d half-window are IDENTICAL between the runs; only the window set
The bar that speaks for an indicator is the grid row with the largest |separation| (ties to the shorter window), so the
DIRECTION shown is FITTED from that row's sign, never imposed — and that same |separation| is what the capture bar is read on.
A leg CAPTURES iff |separation| >= 0.5 AND neither window side's mean is inside the +/-0.06 dead zone. Capturing legs carry a
filled diamond; degenerate legs cannot capture however deep they read.
WHICH SET FITS BETTER is decided by summed capture DEPTH, not headcount, with ties to the coarser (fewer-pin) set. Both greedy
equal-weight keep lists are EMPTY: every candidate made the anchor's own aggregate separation worse, so the frozen rule keeps
gold_v1 ⊂ gold_v2 (same turns, same kinds): gold_v2 REFINES the same target by interpolating the turns between Set A's picks,
so a separation that moves between the two is the granularity speaking, not a contradiction. A window is a scoring target, not
an execution period — no exposure floor, no perfect-strategy oracle.
IN-SAMPLE — a scoring target only, NOT a performance claim. Every separation is the MAXIMUM over a frozen grid, scored against cycle windows derived
from the SAME price history the z-series are built from, so capture counts and depths are a partly-selected UPPER BOUND. No return / Sharpe / trade
count is claimed on this figure.
